about: What `fast-test` runs for a change (see ~/Code/fast-test). Quick steps run on The Dragon; the Rust tests run on The Beast, and a wide change also runs the full suite there. The NixOS VM tests, appliance builds and qualification stay out: by hand or the qualification workflow, when someone asks. So do the signed-seed tests that need a Nix daemon (test_source_policy_seed_cache.py): they run where CI is set, in the release workflow's Nix guest, and The Beast's container sets CI without having Nix, so `full` runs the appliance tests without it.

steps.name: rust
steps.about: The unit tests of the changed modules (src/routes/x.rs runs the tests named routes::x::…), on The Beast: building them compiles the crate.
steps.run: set --; for f in {files}; do m=${f#src/}; m=${m%.rs}; m=${m%/mod}; set -- "$@" "$(printf %s "$m" | sed 's#/#::#g')::"; done; cargo test --locked --lib --bins -- "$@"

steps.name: rust-integration
steps.about: A changed integration test file, on The Beast.
steps.run: set --; for f in {files}; do t=${f#tests/}; set -- "$@" --test "${t%.rs}"; done; cargo test --locked "$@"

steps.name: tools-python
steps.about: The release and qualification tools' Python tests.

full: cargo fmt --all --check && cargo test --locked && env -u CI python3 -B -m unittest discover -s nixos-appliance/tests && python3 -B -m unittest discover -s tools/tests

beast.prepare: apt-get update -qq && apt-get install -y -qq --no-install-recommends jq zstd ripgrep >/dev/null && rustup component add rustfmt
